children.text: T3: Plate between magnets

Two identical long cylindrical rod magnets of radius \(R\) share a vertical symmetry axis and have the same polarity orientation. Their narrow air gap has uniform magnetic field \(\mathbf B=B\hat{\mathbf z}\). The field outside the gap is zero. A large horizontal non-magnetic metal plate is placed in the gap and moved at constant velocity \(v\hat{\mathbf y}\). Its thickness is \(\delta\) and resistivity \(\varrho\).

nodes.alt: Original plate-between-magnets setup: aligned cylindrical magnets of diameter 2R, a thin horizontal metal plate of thickness delta in the gap, field along z and plate velocity along positive y.

children.text: a
Sketch the current streamlines in the plate at a given time, and indicate the axes.
b
Find and plot the current density along the line parallel to \(y\) through the magnets' symmetry axis.
c
Find the horizontal force required to move the plate.

statement.text:
T3: Plate between magnets
Two identical long cylindrical rod magnets of radius \(R\) share a vertical symmetry axis and have the same polarity orientation. Their narrow air gap has uniform magnetic field \(\mathbf B=B\hat{\mathbf z}\). The field outside the gap is zero. A large horizontal non-magnetic metal plate is placed in the gap and moved at constant velocity \(v\hat{\mathbf y}\). Its thickness is \(\delta\) and resistivity \(\varrho\).

a
Sketch the current streamlines in the plate at a given time, and indicate the axes.
b
Find and plot the current density along the line parallel to \(y\) through the magnets' symmetry axis.
c
Find the horizontal force required to move the plate.

children.text: T3: Plate between magnets
a. Steady current pattern

The conventional motional current points along \(\mathbf v\times\mathbf B=+vB\hat{\mathbf x}\). Charges accumulate near the circular field boundary until the current is divergence-free. Ohm's law is \(\mathbf j=(\mathbf E+\mathbf v\times\mathbf B)/\varrho\). The electrostatic field persists outside the magnetic patch, where currents return and close the loops. Streamlines are continuous, do not intersect, and kink at the circular boundary because their tangential component can jump.

nodes.alt: Original current streamlines inside and outside the circular magnetic patch. Axes place positive x downwards and positive y rightwards. Current flows along positive x inside and returns outside in symmetric loops.

children.text: b. Polarized-cylinder construction

Model the electric field as that of a uniformly polarized cylinder with polarization vector \(\mathbf P\). This field is obtained by superposing two slightly displaced oppositely charged cylinders with \(q\mathbf s=-\mathbf P\), then taking their displacement to zero. Gauss's law gives \(\mathbf E_\mathrm{in}=-\mathbf P/(2\epsilon_0)\), and outside, for planar radius vector \(\mathbf r\),
\[\mathbf E_\mathrm{out}=\frac{R^2}{2\epsilon_0}\frac{2\mathbf r(\mathbf r\cdot\mathbf P)-r^2\mathbf P}{r^4}.\]

nodes.alt: Original construction using two oppositely charged overlapping cylinders with displacement s and the resulting polarized-cylinder field, including uniform inner field and dipole-like outer field.

children.text: Match the normal current across \(r=R\). The polarization surface charge \(\sigma=\mathbf P\cdot\hat{\mathbf r}\) must cancel the discontinuity in the normal motional current. This gives \(\mathbf P=\epsilon_0\mathbf v\times\mathbf B\). Therefore
\[\mathbf j_\mathrm{in}=\frac{\mathbf v\times\mathbf B}{2\varrho},\qquad \mathbf j_\mathrm{out}=\frac{R^2}{2\varrho r^4}\left[r^2\mathbf v-2\mathbf r(\mathbf r\cdot\mathbf v)\right]\times\mathbf B.\]
On the requested line \(x=0\), only \(j_x\) is nonzero:
\[j_x(y)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{vB}{2\varrho},&|y|<R,\\-\dfrac{vBR^2}{2\varrho y^2},&|y|>R.\end{cases}\qquad j_y=j_z=0.\]

nodes.alt: Original graph of jx against y: constant positive vB/(2 rho) between minus R and R, a jump to minus vB/(2 rho) just outside both rims, and negative inverse-square tails tending to zero.

children.text: The ideal sharp field boundary permits the tangential-current jumps at the two rims. The inside and outside answer fields specify their open domains.
c. Required pulling force
Only current inside the magnetic patch experiences magnetic force. It is uniform, so integrate \(d\mathbf F=\mathbf j\times\mathbf B\,dV\) over volume \(\pi R^2\delta\):
\[\mathbf F_\mathrm{mag}=-\frac{\pi R^2\delta B^2}{2\varrho}\mathbf v,\qquad \mathbf F_\mathrm{pull}=\frac{\pi R^2\delta B^2v}{2\varrho}\hat{\mathbf y}.\]

Alternatively integrate Joule heating. Inside, \(P_\mathrm{in}=\varrho j_\mathrm{in}^2\pi R^2\delta=\pi R^2\delta v^2B^2/(4\varrho)\). Outside, \(j_\mathrm{out}^2=R^4v^2B^2/(4\varrho^2r^4)\), and integrating over annuli gives the same power. Thus \(F_\mathrm{pull}v=P_\mathrm{in}+P_\mathrm{out}\), confirming the force.
Source notes and validity

The source's current-conservation condition is written with a cross-product loop integral. The intended condition is \(\nabla\cdot\mathbf j=0\), equivalently zero net normal flux through a closed boundary. A separate circulation condition applies to the electric field. Several intermediate signs and dimensional factors in the source are typographical. The final currents and force above satisfy both boundary conditions.

The source also discusses a stepping-magnet Faraday model that happens to reproduce the in-plane current formulas but gives an incorrect electric field away from the plate. It is not a valid derivation of that three-dimensional field. In a correctly transformed continuously moving magnet, surface-charge fields cancel the external induced field. The streamlines outside the patch are circles tangent to the boundary: their tangency follows from \(2\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf r=r^2\), with \(\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf P=0\).

nodes.alt: Original outer-current geometry: family of circular streamlines, a chosen circle centre a, point r, its tangent current vector and radial vector r minus a.

children.text: The assumed current is uniform through the plate thickness. Magnetic diffusion has diffusivity \(\varrho/\mu_0\), and the passage time is of order \(R/v\). Skin depth much greater than \(\delta\) requires \(\varrho R\gg\mu_0v\delta^2\). Original marking tables, the full discussion of the invalid alternative, and its partial-credit limits remain in the PDF.

\[\mathbf j_\mathrm{in}=\frac{\mathbf v\times\mathbf B}{2\varrho},\qquad \mathbf j_\mathrm{out}=\frac{R^2}{2\varrho r^4}\left[r^2\mathbf v-2\mathbf r(\mathbf r\cdot\mathbf v)\right]\times\mathbf B.\]

\[j_x(y)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{vB}{2\varrho},&|y|<R,\\-\dfrac{vBR^2}{2\varrho y^2},&|y|>R.\end{cases}\qquad j_y=j_z=0.\]

The ideal sharp field boundary permits the tangential-current jumps at the two rims. The inside and outside answer fields specify their open domains.

Only current inside the magnetic patch experiences magnetic force. It is uniform, so integrate \(d\mathbf F=\mathbf j\times\mathbf B\,dV\) over volume \(\pi R^2\delta\):

The source's current-conservation condition is written with a cross-product loop integral. The intended condition is \(\nabla\cdot\mathbf j=0\), equivalently zero net normal flux through a closed boundary. A separate circulation condition applies to the electric field. Several intermediate signs and dimensional factors in the source are typographical. The final currents and force above satisfy both boundary conditions.
The source also discusses a stepping-magnet Faraday model that happens to reproduce the in-plane current formulas but gives an incorrect electric field away from the plate. It is not a valid derivation of that three-dimensional field. In a correctly transformed continuously moving magnet, surface-charge fields cancel the external induced field. The streamlines outside the patch are circles tangent to the boundary: their tangency follows from \(2\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf r=r^2\), with \(\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf P=0\).

The assumed current is uniform through the plate thickness. Magnetic diffusion has diffusivity \(\varrho/\mu_0\), and the passage time is of order \(R/v\).
